terms.name: acuerdo ecuménico
notes: The phrase is Doctrina's label for the Joint Declaration (DECISIONS 2026-10-15: "labelled 'acuerdo ecuménico'"), not a term of either church: as a term,. What the document says it is, in both columns (it is signed by both):

es: «Una de las finalidades de la presente Declaración conjunta es demostrar que a partir de este diálogo, las iglesias luterana y católica romana se encuentran en posición de articular una interpretación común de nuestra justificación por la gracia de Dios mediante la fe en Cristo. Cabe señalar que no engloba todo lo que una y otra iglesia enseñan acerca de la justificación, limitándose a recoger el consenso sobre las verdades básicas de dicha doctrina y demostrando que las diferencias subsistentes en cuanto a su explicación, ya no dan lugar a condenas doctrinales.» — DJ 5, texto oficial en español, vatican.va Wayback 2001 capture (2001-02-16) of https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/chrstuni/documents/rc_pc_chrstuni_doc_31101999_cath-luth-joint-declaration_sp.html (the live address returns 404, checked 2026-10-21)

en: "The present Joint Declaration has this intention: namely, to show that on the basis of their dialogue the subscribing Lutheran churches and the Roman Catholic Church are now able to articulate a common understanding of our justification by God's grace through faith in Christ. It does not cover all that either church teaches about justification; it does encompass a consensus on basic truths of the doctrine of justification and shows that the remaining differences in its explication are no longer the occasion for doctrinal condemnations." — DJ 5, https://lutheranworld.org/sites/default/files/2022-02/original_jddj_english.pdf

Note (: that the Reformed confession rejects the distinction is deduced from the quoted sentence, which does not say it; one tradition read through its text for another's term): the Reformed confession is read as rejecting the distinction without using the words: "As there is no sin so small but it deserves damnation; so there is no sin so great, that it can bring damnation upon those who truly repent." — WCF XV.4, WCF-1647 p. 57 area. The Apology uses "mortal sin" polemically (Ap IV (II), Triglot numbering (Kolb–Wengert numbering: not read, ): "they dream that faith can coexist with mortal sin"); a Lutheran definition.

terms.name: de condigno
notes: Catholic: (CEC es/en: no «condigno»; Trent VI not searched for the word today).

Luterana (describing the opponents' distinction, in the Apology): "Their feigning a distinction between meritum congrui and meritum condigni [due merit and true, complete merit] is only an artifice in order not to appear openly to Pelagianize." — Apology, Art. IV (II), Triglot English (bracketed gloss is the Triglot's) (Kolb–Wengert numbering: not read, ); es (traducción asistida por IA, sin revisar por Pedro): «Su invención de una distinción entre meritum congrui y meritum condigni [mérito debido y mérito verdadero y completo] es solo un artificio para no parecer abiertamente pelagianos.» This is the Lutheran account of a scholastic term, not a definition by those who hold it; the site should present it as such.

terms.name: fe formada
notes: Catholic: (CEC es/en: no «fe formada» / "formed faith"; Trent VI says faith «sin esperanza y caridad» does not unite perfectly with Christ, cap. 7 — not quoted here).

Luterana (describing the opponents): "They say that these passages of Scripture, (which speak of faith,) ought to be received as referring to a fides formata, i. e., they do not ascribe justification to faith except on account of love." — Apology, Art. IV (II), Triglot English (Kolb–Wengert numbering: not read, ); es (traducción asistida por IA, sin revisar por Pedro): «Dicen que estos pasajes de la Escritura, que hablan de la fe, deben entenderse referidos a una fides formata, es decir, no atribuyen la justificación a la fe sino a causa del amor.» Same caution as C16.

terms.name: penas temporales / penas debidas por el pecado

entries.quote: «El pecado grave nos priva de la comunión con Dios y por ello nos hace incapaces de la vida eterna, cuya privación se llama la "pena eterna" del pecado. Por otra parte, todo pecado, incluso venial, entraña apego desordenado a las criaturas que es necesario purificar, sea aquí abajo, sea después de la muerte, en el estado que se llama Purgatorio. Esta purificación libera de lo que se llama la "pena temporal" del pecado. Estas dos penas no deben ser concebidas como una especie de venganza, infligida por Dios desde el exterior, sino como algo que brota de la naturaleza misma del pecado.»

entries.quote: "Grave sin deprives us of communion with God and therefore makes us incapable of eternal life, the privation of which is called the 'eternal punishment' of sin. On the other hand every sin, even venial, entails an unhealthy attachment to creatures, which must be purified either here on earth, or after death in the state called Purgatory. This purification frees one from what is called the 'temporal punishment' of sin. These two punishments must not be conceived of as a kind of vengeance inflicted by God from without, but as following from the very nature of sin."

terms.name: obras de supererogación
notes: Reformada: «Los que alcanzan el mas alto grado de obediencia que en esta vida es posible, estan todavia muy léjos de poder hacer obras de supererogacion, ó mas de lo que Dios requiere» — Westminster XVI.4, WCF-1880 (OCR «alcanzau», «obedieiícia», «6» read as «alcanzan», «obediencia», «ó»); "They who in their obedience attain to the greatest height which is possible in this life, are so far from being able to supererogate, and to do more than God requires" — WCF XVI.4, WCF-1647. The clause «más de lo que Dios requiere» is the confession's own gloss of the word.

Luterana: the Apology names "works of supererogation" among the opponents' claims ("they have works of supererogation", Triglot English; Apology article and paragraph not recorded (Kolb–Wengert numbering: not read, )); definition.

entries.quote: «Los tres sacramentos del Bautismo, de la Confirmación y del Orden sacerdotal confieren, además de la gracia, un carácter sacramental o "sello" por el cual el cristiano participa del sacerdocio de Cristo y forma parte de la Iglesia según estados y funciones diversos. Esta configuración con Cristo y con la Iglesia, realizada por el Espíritu, es indeleble (Concilio de Trento: DS 1609); permanece para siempre en el cristiano como disposición positiva para la gracia, como promesa y garantía de la protección divina y como vocación al culto divino y al servicio de la Iglesia. entries.text: Partial: no definition of the phrase, but its source says what the sacrifice is offered for. Trent, Ses. notes: The objecting text names it only: "Honorius, having fallen into the Monothelite heresy, was condemned in the seventh century by the sixth Oecumenical Council as a heretic" — Enc-1895 §XVIII.

Católica, by the doctrine the heresy denied (no definition of the name): «la Iglesia confesó en el sexto Concilio Ecuménico que Cristo posee dos voluntades y dos operaciones naturales, divinas y humanas, no opuestas, sino cooperantes» — CEC 475,; "at the sixth ecumenical council, Constantinople III in 681, the Church confessed that Christ possesses two wills and two natural operations, divine and human" — CCC 475,. A definition of «monotelismo».
Note: heresies belong to the shared universe (); a neutral definition, if wanted, goes there, not in a tradition's voice.

terms.name: arriana
notes: The objecting text names it only: "the Pope Liberius, in the fourth century, subscribed an Arian confession" — Enc-1895 §XVIII.

Católica, what Nicaea condemned: «condenó a Arrio que afirmaba que "el Hijo de Dios salió de la nada" (Concilio de Nicea I: DS 130) y que sería "de una substancia distinta de la del Padre"» — CEC 465,; "condemned Arius, who had affirmed that the Son of God 'came to be from things that were not' and that he was 'from another substance' than that of the Father" — CCC 465,. Same note as E2 (shared universe).
